title: mysql driver backend config
description: Schema for the config: block under a backend entry whose driver is mysql (MariaDB 10.11+, MySQL 8). The controller connects with the admin account below; every database and user it manages starts with namePrefix, and it refuses names outside it. See docs/mysql.md for the grants the admin account needs and why CREATE USER makes the prefix the security boundary.

host.description: Server host name or IP, without scheme or port, e.g. mysql.mysql.svc.cluster.local. Also written to access Secrets (host, jdbcUrl, url).

port.description: Server port. Also written to access Secrets.

adminUser.description: The controller's account. Must not start with namePrefix. envsubst:"true" - supports ${VAR} interpolation at controller startup.

adminPassword.description: The controller's password; use ${VAR} interpolation from a Secret-sourced env var rather than a literal. envsubst:"true".

namePrefix.description: Every database and user the driver creates or touches starts with this prefix; Buckety names (spec.name) must resolve to it, e.g. b_${namespace}_${name}. The admin account's database grant is scoped to the same prefix (GRANT ALL ON `b\_%`.*). Fixed for the backend's lifetime: resources stamped under one prefix are refused under another.

userHost.description: Host part of created accounts ('user'@'<userHost>'). Must also admit the controller's own address: the driver verifies passwords and grants by logging in as each user. Changing it moves accesses to new accounts on their next reconcile and drops the old ones.

tls.description: Present (even as {}) to require verified TLS on the controller's connections. Absent means plaintext. Does not add REQUIRE SSL to created users; enforce TLS for consumers server-side with require_secure_transport.

caFile.description: PEM bundle (mounted into the controller Pod) to verify the server certificate with. System roots when omitted.

serverName.description: Name to verify in the server certificate. Defaults to host.
